solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foolish Hindu god returned flower

indicators.note: something returned is sent back the way it came, so the two words are read from the end

parts.note: foolish means silly
Rama is a Hindu god, an incarnation of Vishnu

explanation.surface: A daft deity sends back a bloom he was given.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaryllis is a showy bulb plant grown for its trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Country roads run up underneath a weapons store

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece underneath another comes after it
in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lanes are narrow country roads
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Rural roads climb up to an armoury hidden below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LANES + R to give RSENAL, which sits 'underneath' A.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a building where arms and ammunition are kept or made.

clue.text: Assert without proof everyone European has good English

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone claims, unproven, that every European speaks fine English.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim something is so without yet having shown it.

clue.text: Unusually achy time in sailing boat

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of achy appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Feeling oddly sore for a spell while out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a light vessel with sails, used for racing or cruising.

clue.text: Hawaiian garland that is left over

indicators.note: turned over, the letters are read in the reverse order

parts.note: IE (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A flower necklace from Hawaii that's been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns IEL round; 'left over' looks like one phrase meaning surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is the ring of flowers placed around a visitor's neck in Hawaii.

clue.text: Donuts were as awful as some Chinese food

indicators.note: awful means badly made, so the letters of these three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: The doughnuts tasted as bad as a takeaway from a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet-and-sour is a style of Chinese cooking with a sugary, vinegary sauce.

clue.text: Measure encountered by Her Majesty

parts.note: encountered means met
ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A step taken when someone meets the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is a gauge that records quantity, as with gas or electricity.

clue.text: Turned out in numbers in service for Italian leader that's died

parts.note: Mass is a church service
pro means for, in favour of
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini, Italy's fascist leader

explanation.surface: Crowds flocked to a church service for a dead Italian chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian leader' wants to be I; it is DUCE, Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made on a factory scale are churned out in large quantities.

clue.text: Current keeping river hot and humid

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: current means topical, of present interest

explanation.surface: A sticky climate and a flowing stream of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a flow of water beside 'river', but it means topical.
explanation.definitionFit: Climates near the equator are typically sweltering and muggy.

clue.text: Choosing to put into power four in south-east

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed inside the other

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone into office
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A quartet in the south-east decide who will govern.
explanation.definitionFit: A selective person picks carefully, choosing only some things.

clue.text: Distressed about clubs making a number of goals

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: distressed can mean sore, upset or aggrieved
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Fans of the clubs upset over the goal tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests football teams but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The score is the tally of goals each side has scored in a match.

clue.text: Club near empty Thames vessel

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: A club beside a London river, and a boat moored there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks like a boat on the Thames; it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue for drinking and dancing late at night.

clue.text: Cooperate with what theatre may put on before dance

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: a theatre stages a play
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Working together on a theatre show staged ahead of a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work along with others.

clue.text: Remember being concerned with visit

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to call is to pay a visit

explanation.surface: Thinking back on what a visit was about.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind.

clue.text: Resistance in European nation is a joint problem

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: Spain is a European nation
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A wartime resistance movement in Spain is a shared trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint problem' reads as a shared difficulty; it is a twisted ankle or wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrenched ankle or wrist is an injury to a body joint.

clue.text: Former name for particle, one out of place

indicators.note: out of means the following piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: position means place
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An old label for a particle that is displaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' looks like one phrase meaning misplaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Positon was an early name for the positron, the electron's antiparticle.

clue.text: A poem of Byron delights

indicators.note: of means made of part of, so the letters are drawn from inside Byron delights

explanation.surface: A verse by Lord Byron gives pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondel is a short verse form with a recurring refrain.

clue.text: Fine food shop right to take promissory notes? Crazy

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, selling fine foods
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A gourmet shop agreeing to accept IOUs must be mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone delirious is wildly excited or deranged, beside themselves.

clue.text: Grub around small hen-house

indicators.note: around means one piece goes about the other

parts.note: to grub is to root, dig about

explanation.surface: Scratching for food around a little chicken coop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' reads as food for hens; it is a verb meaning dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch or shelter where poultry rest at night.

clue.text: I had a house in an American state

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls owning a home in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a north-western state of the USA, famed for potatoes.

clue.text: Doctor can upset agreement

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician may be able to overturn a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal pact, especially between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Old horse has problem dropping head

indicators.note: dropping head means losing the first letter

parts.note: a snag is a problem

explanation.surface: An aged horse has trouble keeping its head up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is a worn-out or inferior horse.

clue.text: Tanker, a steam-generating vessel, not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a boiler is a vessel that heats water into steam

explanation.surface: An old ship comparing itself to a steam boiler.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil, especially to refuel others at sea.

clue.text: Dilating abnormally, I injected heart drug

indicators.note: injected means one piece is put inside the other
abnormally means not in the usual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient's vessels widen oddly after a dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abnormally' turns DILATING into DIGTALIN, and 'injected' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalin, from foxglove, is a medicine that strengthens the heartbeat.
